findings.where: /museum/network-onchain headline and all page titles · default · all viewports · en-US; How this is checked · contract checks
findings.observation: Resolved. The h1 reads 'The Museum's records, from a test preview'; the page titles read '6529 Network Museum, on-chain preview' and 'Texts, 6529 Network Museum on-chain preview', which name the preview, not a chain read, and sit under a banner that says nothing was read from Sepolia or mainnet. The registry check now reads 'The fixture holds the 589 records of the Museum's release: Passed', a fact the fixture run supports; the three unrun contract checks say 'Not checked: read from fixtures'.
findings.consequence: The first thing a reviewer reads still claims a chain read, and one Passed mark states a fact about a registry that was not queried.
findings.change: In fixture mode make the h1 'The Museum, from a test preview' (or 'The Museum's records') and the titles 'Preview from local fixtures'; show the registry-holds-589-records check as 'Not checked: read from fixtures' (or reword it to 'The release lists 589 records' if that is what ran). Keep 'read from the chain' for the registry-present branch.
findings.acceptance_check: With fixtures, no h1, page title or Passed mark states or implies a chain or registry read; the live branch copy is unchanged.

findings.where: record routes and index Releases section · default · all viewports · en-US
findings.observation: Resolved. The block now reads 'The values the release's record list gives for this record. Publication time, order and publisher exist only once the record is on-chain.' No record page shows Published, Sequence, Publisher or 'as stored'; the release row reads '403 records and 186 texts' with no Sealed time.
findings.consequence: Synthesized publication dates and sequence numbers read as real on-chain history that a reviewer would cite.
findings.change: In fixture mode label the block 'Values from the fixture' and show Published, Sealed, Sequence and Publisher as 'Not on-chain yet' or omit them; keep 'as stored' for live reads only.
findings.acceptance_check: No record page or release row shows a Published or Sealed time, or the 'as stored' line, unless the value came from the registry.

findings.where: record-text-essay, texts, record-observation, record-declaration · default · all viewports · en-US
findings.observation: Resolved. No Source path field, no 'declaration' Museum ID, no RFC8785_JCS code and no UUID URL appear on the 15 routes; text groups are headed 'Accession', 'Proposed gift: Conflict at Its Edges' and 'Acquisition program'; the observation is titled 'Status observation, Aug 8, 2026' and shows 'Page on 6529.io'. 'WP-3 source register' and 'WP-1 schema and vocabulary dependencies' remain as titles, but they are the published record titles and shown as recorded.
findings.consequence: Visitors meet working-package codes and file paths as headings and titles and cannot tell what 6529NM-PG-2026-001 or WP-3 is.
findings.change: Drop Source path from the visible fields (keep it in the copyable JSON). Name the proposed-gift groups by the work, e.g. 'Proposed gift: Conflict at Its Edges' and 'Proposed gift: Themes and Variations #210'. Title observations by what they observed ('Status observation, 8 Aug 2026') with the ID secondary. Show the link target as a labelled link ('Wave drop on 6529.io'). Remove the raw RFC8785_JCS code and the 'declaration' ID from visible rows.
findings.acceptance_check: No repository path, WP-/PG- code or bare UUID URL appears as a heading, title or field value on the 15 routes; text group headings name an object.

findings.where: texts and record-work-portrait · default · all viewports · en-US
findings.observation: Partly fixed: Take the Key! now shows Acquisition 'Keys and Gates' once. The texts jump list still has 'Acquisition program: Keys and Gates', 'Acquisition program · works: Keys and Gates' and 'Acquisition program · artists: Keys and Gates', which differ only after a middle dot.
findings.consequence: A reader scanning the jump list sees three near-identical entries.
findings.change: Show one 'Acquisition' line when acquisition and program have the same title; label the jump-list entries 'Keys and Gates: program texts / works / artists'.
findings.acceptance_check: Take the Key! shows Keys and Gates once in About this record; texts jump entries differ in their leading words, not only in a middle dot.

findings.where: record-work and record-work-portrait · default · all viewports · en-US
findings.observation: Improved: the caption now has the credit line plus one page line, 'CC BY-NC 4.0, with some uses refused. Full rights statement'. The license is still named twice in a row (credit line ends 'Licensed under CC BY-NC 4.0.'), the page line does not say which uses are refused, and at 390 px the caption runs five lines (evidence/record-work-390x844-02.png). The credit line itself is record text and is shown as recorded.
findings.consequence: Minor repetition; the reader must open the rights statement to learn the limits.
findings.change: Replace the page line with 'Attribution required; noncommercial use only. Full rights statement', or drop the license name from it.
findings.acceptance_check: The page-authored caption line does not repeat the license name and states the main limit; caption is three lines or fewer at 390 px beyond the credit line.

findings.where: record-work-portrait, record-work-noimage, record-decision, record-object · default · all viewports · en-US
findings.observation: Resolved by the run record's scope: Medium caveats, 'Casey REAS' in the credit line, artist name forms and the decision Statement (with its ISO acceptance date) are text inside published records, which pages show as recorded. Any correction belongs in the source records, not the page.
findings.consequence: Mixed caveats, handles and casing make the record look unfinished and inconsistent across pages.
findings.change: Keep Medium to the medium and show caveats on a separate 'Note' line; use the artist's display name on every page (handle in parentheses once); set the Statement to a short sentence ('7 objects accessioned by donation, accepted 1 Aug 2026') with the numbers as links. If the source record is the cause, fix the record, not the page.
findings.acceptance_check: Medium holds only medium; one name per artist across work, artist and texts pages; the decision statement is two lines or fewer at 1440 px.

findings.observation: Resolved. The opening paragraph reads 'holds 13 works in its collection and has selected 16 more through its acquisitions and programs. 186 texts describe them.' with verification second; the section is headed 'Decisions, rights and observations'.
findings.consequence: A visitor who wants to find a work gets a verification explanation first, and the label 'Object records' misdescribes its contents.
findings.change: Lead with a sentence of real counts ('13 works in the collection, 16 selected for Keys and Gates, 186 texts') and put the verification sentence second. Rename 'Object records' to 'Decisions, rights and condition reports'.
findings.acceptance_check: The first paragraph names the collection and its counts; the 'Object records' heading names the record kinds it contains.
